content:
maria: Quick question — for the private deploy audit, where should WAF events live? Compliance wants them in Splunk HEC and we also need KMS key IDs surfaced for correlation with encrypted archives. cc @chris @ben :eyes:
chris: Today WAF -> syslog-ng -> forwarder -> Splunk HEC. No KMS metadata in payloads yet.
ben: We can enrich at the forwarder with key id. Forwarder already authenticates to keystore service so add a small metadata fetch.
sam: Careful with perms. Giving forwarder keystore read is risky. Prefer a minimal metadata-only endpoint that returns key_id only, no decrypt.
maria: Agreed. Proposal: forwarder hits internal endpoint `/keystore/key-metadata?alias=...` (role: keystore.metadata-reader). It returns only `{key_id: "alias/priv-deploy-01"}` and we stamp logs. No key material leaves keystore.
nathan_ops: Ok. We'll need an IAM change: grant `keystore.metadata-reader` to forwarder SA. Who opens the PR?
ben: I'll open the IAM PR. Also we should attach `request_id` tracing so Splunk can join WAF events with keystore calls.
chris: For ingestion use JSON fields: `request_id`, `waf_rule`, `key_id`, `src_ip`, `action`. Example message from forwarder:
{ "ts": "2026-04-12T14:22:01Z", "request_id": "req_3f9a1", "waf_rule": "sql_injection_block", "action": "blocked", "key_id": "alias/priv-deploy-01", "src_ip": "10.2.4.8" }
maria: Two follow-ups: (1) retention — regulated customers need 2y. (2) evidence we didn't leak keys in the recent WAF upgrade vuln triage.
sam: Splunk supports per-index retention. Ops: create index `priv_audit_waf` with 2y retention.
nathan_ops: Will do. Which CVE are we mapping to this review? I saw an alert about header parsing.
maria: CVE-2026-1029 (the WAF header-parsing vuln). We patched last week. Need proof the patch didn't leak key material or headers stored in plaintext.
ben: I pulled post-patch logs — no key material present, only `key_id`. Forwarder logs show `GET /keystore/key-metadata?alias=priv-deploy-01` 200.
chris: Let's add a small audit runbook entry with reproducible evidence steps: 1) export Splunk query for events with `key_id` and `request_id` range; 2) show forwarder call logs to keystore; 3) show keystore access logs (which SA used metadata-reader); 4) include KMS CMK rotation history and archive manifest.
maria: Good. Add to private-deploy runbook and attach the Splunk snippet.
ben: Adding now. Splunk query (draft): `index=priv_audit_waf sourcetype=json key_id=alias/priv-deploy-01 | stats count by waf_rule, action`
sam: Also update RBAC ticket with CI smoke tests that assert forwarder cannot call Decrypt. Have CI call both metadata and decrypt endpoints with the forwarder SA token.
nathan_ops: I'll add infra-ci tests and gate the IAM PR on CI passing.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3957 — WAF upgrade review (assigned: @maria, @ben).
maria: Ops, make sure Splunk index exports to long-term archive (S3 with SSE-KMS) and include CMK ARN in `archive_manifest.json` so auditors can tie logs to keys.
chris: We'll use envelope-encryption with account CMK and include manifest with `cmk_arn`, `start_ts`, `end_ts`.
ben: I'll add a sample manifest to the runbook and link the IAM PR.
maria: Thanks. If nobody objects I'll merge IAM PR and update runbook. :thumbsup:
sam: No objections.
chris: Go ahead.
ben: PR link: https://git.company/repo/pulls/482 (rbac: forwarder -> keystore.metadata-reader)
maria: I'll update the compliance checklist and upload evidence to the runbook after CI passes. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
